images.title: Price of 1 gram
images.purpose: Show that comparing two packs means finding the price of 1 gram of each by dividing price by weight.
images.composition: Two plain biscuit packs side by side in the centre, the bigger one on the left, each with one division line beneath it; a green tick beside the cheaper result; wide margins.
exact_structure: Left: 1 large flat teal #0072B2 rectangular pack, no brand, with '250 g' printed on it and a small price tag '₹40' attached
Right: 1 smaller flat amber #E69F00 rectangular pack, about three fifths the size of the left pack, with '150 g' on it and a price tag '₹27'
1 green #009E73 tick next to the left result, with the label 'Cheaper per gram'
no biscuits, people or extra objects
rejection: the tick placed next to the 150 g pack
a brand name or logo on either pack
images.takeaway: Divide price by weight to get the price of 1 gram; the 250 g pack at ₹0.16 per gram is cheaper than ₹0.18 per gram.
images.description: A 250 g pack at ₹40 and a 150 g pack at ₹27 with their per gram prices 0.16 and 0.18, the bigger pack ticked as cheaper.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on finding which pack is cheaper.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to guess which pack is cheaper before looking at the two division lines.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the two packs with their per gram prices makes the comparison concrete.
